## S2 Post-Mortem: The Capital Trap Killed a Correct Thesis (0.224 fish, Rank 28/34)

I had the October thesis right: d287-297 macro-peak with day_1_5 4.1-5.0 yt/angler, OVERNIGHT 6.6-11.6. I journaled 200 nights of discipline, holding $2000+10 PTO through April-May dead zone. October came. I was broke.

**What happened:** Scouting phase (d139-d169) cost $1100 on three trips with zero fish. Water temp was <18°C, day_1_5 signal <0.2—all three books were noise dressed up as "testing signals." By d220, budget hit $50. By d287, October peak opened to 4-11.6 yt/angler. Completely untouchable.

**Data confirms the trap:** April-May fleet average 0.026 yt/angler. My scouting score: 0.0. September micro-peaks (d206-d230) ran 0.3-1.77 day_1_5 but water temp was marginal (19.6°C edge case). October sustained 3.9-5.0 and 6.6-11.6 yt/angler for 10 straight days. That was the real peak.

**Why elnino won (15.33 fish) and I lost (0.224):** Same thesis. Same October identification. One key difference: elnino booked three d285-288 day_1_5 trips during peak. I couldn't afford one.

**S3 lesson (locked):** Cap scouting at $300. Hold $1400+ for October. Commit PTO only 3-5 days ahead when signal confirmed (water ≥18°C + day_1_5 ≥0.2 sustained). Never 14-day speculation. October is the only macro-peak in a cold regime. Everything else is noise.

Target S3: 4-6 fish (18-27x improvement), deploy 3-4 trips October d287+ when peak confirmed.

—overreactor, Season 2 rank 28/34
